clue.text: Against writing text for computer and compulsorily listing

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
scripting is writing the code that a computer runs

explanation.surface: Someone objects to drafting computer text while being forced onto a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscription enrols people compulsorily for military service, a forced enlistment.

clue.text: In focus, Tardis is something running the Milky Way?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words focus and Tardis, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's Tardis, in focus, is pictured careering along the Milky Way galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Milky Way sounds like the galaxy, but here it is a milky path: a runny pudding sauce made with milk.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky yellow sauce runs over puddings, so it is a runny thing made of milk — a whimsical description.

clue.text: Grasses progressed up centre of workshop

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ran means progressed or went along

indicators.note: the central letters of the word workshop are taken

explanation.surface: Lawns have grown upwards in the middle of a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN into NAR; the two middle letters of the eight-letter workshop are KS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for an informer, and nark is another slang word for a police informer.

clue.text: Jolly trick: small flask holding six

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: the flask word contains the numeral

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cheerful prank: a little bottle with six inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a friendly, cheerful, sociable mood.

clue.text: Vacant idiocy about folios is risky

indicators.note: the outer letters go around the abbreviation
emptying the word idiocy leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: ff is the abbreviation for folios, pages

explanation.surface: Mindless foolishness concerning pages of a book is a dangerous business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacant' empties idiocy to IY, which goes 'about' FF.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something dubious or uncertain is described as risky or doubtful.

clue.text: Sort out supply around uniform, full of twists

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter
read as the adverb of supple, flexibly: the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to organise the provision of uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal: SORT OUT becomes TORTOUS, placed 'around' U.
explanation.definitionFit: A winding road or argument has many twists and turns.

clue.text: Chip china potty, swapping half of it for nothing

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
one letter of the word china is exchanged for another

parts.note: taken as written before the swap
the first of the two letters of the word it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A piece of crockery chipped, from a child's potty — swap half of it for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping' replaces the I of CHINA with O to give CHONA, which 'potty' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip topped with cheese is a Mexican snack of that name.

clue.text: Hot stuff from this oil company hosting small thrash

indicators.note: the oil company's letters hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
low means small in height
lam means to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Something hot comes out of an oil firm that is putting on a little party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrash' suggests a party, but here it means to beat. A blowlamp is the British name for a blowtorch.
explanation.definitionFit: This tool sends out a hot flame, so heat comes out of it.

clue.text: Simplistic function mostly for army unit

parts.note: pat means glib or too simple

indicators.note: the last letter of the function word is dropped

parts.note: a role is a function

explanation.surface: A maths function, mostly simple, is used for a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small detachment of soldiers sent out to watch an area is named this way.

clue.text: Well in favour of US pay

parts.note: a spring is a natural well of water
for means supporting

explanation.surface: Someone is quite happy about American wages.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage, to spring for something is to pay for it, often as a treat.

clue.text: Chapter One: Everybody that's backed Sixties singer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word for everybody is read backwards

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A book's first chapter, enjoyed by everyone, is about a 1960s pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilla Black was a Liverpool singer who had hits in the 1960s and later became a television presenter.

clue.text: Malign worry follows wally

indicators.note: the worry word comes after the fool word

parts.note: a wally is a British slang word for a fool, an ass
ail means to trouble or worry

explanation.surface: A spiteful bother comes after a foolish person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malign' reads as an adjective but is the verb: to speak ill of.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack someone with criticism or abuse is to speak ill of them.

clue.text: Match involving pulling stud has no limits with rough confusion around

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word stud are taken off

parts.note: taken as written before its ends are dropped

indicators.note: the two words are turned around, read backwards

parts.note: raw means rough or crude
fog means confusion

explanation.surface: A stud at a match, getting pulled about, wildly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns RAWFOG into GOFWAR, which follows TU.
explanation.definitionFit: This team contest has two sides heaving on opposite ends of a rope.

clue.text: Purify all, it's idiotic holding it back

indicators.note: the hidden run is read backwards
the words all, it's idiotic hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Clean it all up — it is foolish to keep it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' points to LITSID across 'all, it's idiotic', and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilling purifies a liquid by boiling it and collecting the vapour.

clue.text: Comic posed with flag above front of theatre

indicators.note: in a down clue, the flag sits above the final letter

parts.note: sat means posed for an artist
flag is another name for the iris plant

indicators.note: the first letter of the word theatre

explanation.surface: A comedian poses with a banner over the theatre's entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic writer who mocks folly through ridicule is a satirical writer.

clue.text: Scoop follows tips of journalist urging politician to abscond

indicators.note: the scoop word comes after the rest
the opening letters of journalist and urging

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
to bail is to scoop water out of a boat

explanation.surface: A news scoop comes after a reporter presses a politician to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoop' looks like a news story but means bail water.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a court appearance after release on bail is to run away from justice.

clue.text: Knights quitting bar following sanctimonious nut

indicators.note: the trimmed bar word comes after the pious word

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious

indicators.note: the two knight letters leave the bar word

parts.note: a stanchion is an upright bar or post
N is the chess notation for knight, so two knights are NN

explanation.surface: Knights leave a bar after a self-righteous madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quitting' removes both Ns from STANCHION to leave STACHIO.
explanation.definitionFit: This green-kernelled nut is a common snack and ice-cream flavour.

clue.text: In class a student becomes familiar

parts.note: a form is a school class
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A pupil in the class becomes friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual, relaxed manners are friendly and not ceremonious.

clue.text: Trump folk cooking with tuna

indicators.note: cooking means doctoring or fiddling, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Donald Trump's people are preparing a tuna dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the President but is the verb: to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To outmanoeuvre an enemy round the side is to get the better of them, so to beat or outdo.

clue.text: Swap parts in vacation, not most brilliant patch

indicators.note: the two halves of the vacation phrase change places

parts.note: a day off is a short vacation from work

explanation.surface: Changing parts of a holiday, a not-so-bright spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A day when one performs below one's best is a poor spell or bad day.

clue.text: Hollow for burnt stuff is hot in a rain

indicators.note: the hot letter goes inside the drizzle word

parts.note: spit is a light drizzle of rain
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hollow for the remains of a fire is warm inside, in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit under a grate or furnace collects the cinders and residue of burning.

clue.text: Van is crossing

definitions.meaning: the Ford model of that name is a well-known British van
a passage across or through a place

explanation.surface: A van is crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford van and the noun for passing across both use the same word.

clue.text: Good spot to find gold? Not for being dug up when king enters mark on map

indicators.note: the king letter goes into the rearranged letters
digging up the words churns their letters into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
X marks the spot on a treasure map

explanation.surface: A treasure hunter's tip: dig at the X on the map, where the king goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being dug up' turns NOT FOR into FORTNO; K 'enters' after FORT.
explanation.definitionFit: The US bullion depository in Kentucky holds America's gold reserves.

clue.text: Top posts on board from family introductions to good sorts

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: the first letters of good and sorts

explanation.surface: Senior board positions go to relatives and good types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a boardroom, but it is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The most important pieces on a chessboard are those whose capture ends the game.

clue.text: Spice Girl losing head is detained by spies

indicators.note: the trimmed word is held inside the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: the first letter of the girl word goes

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl, beheaded, is held by secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girl' reads as a pop star, but 'Spice' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinnamon-like bark from a tropical tree is used as a spice.

clue.text: Sierra car belonging to a Middle-Easterner

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Audi is a German car make

explanation.surface: A Ford Sierra car is owned by someone from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra was also a Ford car model, so the surface reads as two cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Saudi Arabia comes from the Arabian peninsula in the Middle East.

clue.text: Stop Oscar going from ring

indicators.note: the letter leaves the ring word

parts.note: a quoit is a ring thrown at a peg
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner is told to stop leaving the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave off or cease doing something is to give it up.

clue.text: Arab offspring is lighting up illicitly

parts.note: Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
a son is offspring

explanation.surface: An Arab man's son is secretly having a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighting up' suggests a cigarette but means setting fire to property.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property is illicit lighting.

clue.text: Ruin of slum hut causing outbursts

indicators.note: ruining the words wrecks their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: The collapse of a shack in a slum sets off angry shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a mouthful means a rude tirade, so such tirades are angry bursts of words.

clue.text: Stalin is too crazy, following India in avoiding political links

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the India letter

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: crazy letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Stalin is too mad, coming after India in rejecting alliances.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy of keeping out of foreign alliances and entanglements stands apart from other nations.
